products.name: Freepik AI
products.note: Stock image AI generation; commercial licensing; EU-hosted; content moderation

reading.body:
Freepik's AI product is a stock image generator with commercial licensing, EU hosting, and content moderation, which places it in the licensing and compliance layer of image generation rather than the compute race.

The pattern here is a company selling generated images as licensed stock. Commercial licensing means the output is meant to be used in someone else's product, so the legal terms matter as much as the model. EU hosting and content moderation are the two facts that shape where the work runs and what it is allowed to produce.

For AI specifically, this is a reminder that not every image product competes on scale. A stock image generator serves customers who need rights to the output, and that need is met by licensing terms and hosting location, not by the largest possible cluster. The data does not say which models Freepik uses, how much compute it buys, where its servers draw power, or how large its customer base is. It also does not give any dates for when these capabilities launched or changed.

What the data does not cover is the infrastructure underneath. There is no mention of data centers, power contracts, or chip supply, so nothing here supports a claim about Freepik's compute footprint. The entry is a product description, not an operations record, and it should be read that way.
